news.title: Amputee Football World Cup: Ghana seek winning response against Colombia after opening-day setback
news.lede: Ghana’s Black Challenge will be determined to bounce back from their opening-day disappointment when they take on Colombia in their second Group D encounter at the 2026 WAFF Amputee Football World Cup on Sunday, November 15, 2026. The Ghanaian side will be eager to put their campaign back on track following a 2-0 defeat to former world champions Angola in their opening fixture on Saturday. Head coach Stephen Richard Obeng and his charges now face a crucial test against Colombia at Santa Lucia 1 in Mexico, knowing that a positive result is essential to keeping their hopes of advancing to the next stage alive. Having suffered an early setback, the Black Challenge will be keen to rediscover their rhythm, sharpen their attacking threat and demonstrate greater resilience as they seek to get their campaign up and running.

news.title: Romario slams Ancelotti after Brazil defeat against Japan: ‘Take your things and go’
news.lede: Carlo Ancelotti is facing backlash in Brazil after leading the Selecao to a 3-2 defeat against Japan earlier this weekend, and 1994 World Cup winner Romario has been among the Italian’s loudest critics: ‘Take your things and go’. Brazil were defeated 3-2 by Japan in a friendly in Singapore earlier this weekend, a game that saw Ancelotti sent off for running onto the pitch to protest Japan’s 91st-minute winner. He felt that Joao Gomes had been fouled in the build-up to Tatsuhiro Sakamoto’s late decider. This comes after a disappointing display at the 2026 World Cup, which saw Brazil knocked out at the round of 16 stage after a 2-1 defeat by Norway.

news.title: Football: Dauntless Moriyasu topples another giant before signing off
news.lede: TOKYO - With the curtain closing on his tenure as Japan manager, Hajime Moriyasu produced one final win over a football powerhouse, emblematic of his drama-filled eight-plus years in charge. Seeking revenge for their World Cup loss to Brazil in North America this summer, Japan again led at halftime on Saturday in Singapore but refused to retreat this time, securing a late 3-2 win. Japan played with a back four throughout rather than the back three that effectively became a back five in June as Brazil pinned them back after halftime. The setup allowed more players to stay high up the pitch and execute Moriyasu's plan to create more chances and challenge aggressively.

news.title: Black Challenge lose 2-0 to Angola in Amputee Football World Cup Opener
news.lede: Ghana’s Black Challenge began their WAFF Amputee Football World Cup campaign with a 2-0 defeat to Angola on Saturday, November 14, 2026, at San Martin in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico. Ghana conceded one goal in each half as Angola took the points in the Group game. The Black Challenge held their shape well in the early stages, but Angola broke the deadlock before half-time to take a 1-0 lead into the break. Angola added a second goal in the second half to seal the 2-0 win, despite a spirited effort from the Ghana side.
